clauses.evidence: Directed right turn of -58.5 deg (heading within +/-1 deg until 52.95 s, -40.9 deg by 53.80 s, -58.5 deg by 55.43 s); the later -36 deg yaw pulse at 56.5-58.3 s is a separate maneuver and not added.

The person ahead in the new corridor at 55.28 s (blonde, dark backpack, jeans) is first seen at the front-camera right edge at 53.09 s, after braking and at turn onset; before the turn the right half of the front view is blocked by a crossing pedestrian, and the frontleft (looks front-right) frame at header 52.58 s shows other people, so side visibility of this same person before the turn is not established.
clauses.clause: Same pedestrian visible at side before turn

clauses.evidence: Crowded hall: the orange-jacket pedestrian who is also ahead after the turn (in_corridor cluster 3.42 m at -15.5 deg, 53.78 s) crossed the forward path left-to-right at ~1-2 m during 50.5-52.5 s, so she fails; for the blonde candidate, her image shift from right edge to centre-left over 53.09-53.85 s roughly matches the -41 deg yaw, but without her pre-turn track a pedestrian crossing cannot be excluded.

The corridor entry at ~53.8 s comes ~1.1 s later; the slowdown overlaps a close crossing pedestrian.
clauses.clause: Compare slowdown onset with geometric transition

gradeNote: Turn and slowdown timing are measured, but same-person side visibility before the turn and the no-crossing condition for the candidate are unresolved in a dense crowd; the other person who ends up ahead crossed the path.
coverage: odom ~16 Hz, velodyne ~10 Hz, front 30 Hz, body cams 4.5 Hz with ~0.45 s capture latency; no gaps; baseline 50.5-52.5 s fully covered (filtered speed 1.19-1.51 m/s).

clauses.evidence: He crosses the robot's original heading line himself: lidar puts him at ~+55 deg left, ~1.8 m at 31.21 s, then in the corridor at 1.77 m / -5.4 deg at 32.22 s (yaw +16.7 deg), then at 2.09 m / -43.9 deg at 32.72 s (yaw ~+37 deg). That is ~100 deg of bearing change against ~37 deg of yaw, and forward motion would push a static left object further left, so his own left-to-right walk drives the corridor entry.
clauses.clause: Corridor occupancy changes because robot reorients, not pedestrian crossing

Close-range lidar clusters near the left railing are partly merged (1.64 m cluster, 3.76 m extent at 31.3 s), so the pre-turn bearing is approximate.

gradeNote: Near miss: a stationary person is swept into the corridor by a ~174 deg in-place turn and slowing precedes it, but before the turn he was behind the robot, not at its side. He also appears to be the robot handler (holding a controller), which weakens 'pedestrian'. Counting only the post-39 s part of the turn would split one maneuver, so it was not done.
coverage: odom ~16 Hz, velodyne ~10 Hz, front 30 Hz, back/left cams 4.5 Hz with ~0.45 s capture latency; no gaps. The corridor box is truncated by the landing wall at ~2 m, and other people (masked woman, man in black) move nearby during the turn.
